messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High 5xx rate and tail latency for inference-prod-usw2:az1a detected by synthetic checks (5m window). Creating incident thread and paging oncall. Automated severity: SEV-2.

anna_oncall: On it. I’m oncall for USW2. Pulling dashboards.

sanjay: Seeing the same in logs — connection resets and increased retransmits from nodes in az1a. KVCACHE miss rate spiked ~08:12 UTC.

maria: Customer-facing trend: hosted API error rate up to 3.2% overall for region, but spikes to ~12% when requests land on az1a. Most errors are 502/504.

josh: Can we steer traffic off az1a? Any healthy spare capacity in other AZs?

anna_oncall: Trying soft-steer via route policy to prefer az1b/c. Running quick check: az1b has ~65% GPU pool utilization, az1c ~40%. Steer might succeed but risk of cross-AZ egress increase. Initiating canary steer to 5% traffic.

incident-bot: Runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/az-egress-degrade> — recommended steps: check instance network plane, ENI resets, NAT/egress throttles, and option to enable failover routing.

katie: Logs show kernel rx-drop counters incrementing on several g5 nodes in az1a. Example from node gpu-az1a-07: 
```
netdev: eth0 rx dropped: 1243
dmesg: rx kthread timeout, interface reset
```

anna_oncall: That matches packet drop symptoms. Could be NIC firmware regression or host-level backpressure. I'm asking infra to triage host-level NIC metrics.

maria: CS update — Ryan, flagging impacted customers: two enterprise tenants in USW2 on Dedicated reservations might see increased latency and occasional failures for traffic pinned to az1a. They'll want an update.

cs_ryan: Acknowledged. I’ll prepare a short customer note: "We’re mitigating an AZ-level networking degradation in US West 2, routing traffic away from the affected nodes and monitoring. No data exposure. Will update in 30m."

josh: Canary steering to 5% succeeded with no errors. Bumping to 25% now. Observability: 5xx rate in non-az1a drops to baseline, but az1a still noisy.

incident-bot: Pager escalation: SEV-2 -> ENG-SRE pager if failures persist after 30m.

anna_oncall: Starting active mitigation sequence: (1) Mark az1a GPU nodes draining for new inference allocations (taint + no-schedule for batch jobs). (2) Enable region-wide fallback model for small requests to reduce per-token pressure. (3) Open AWS case for NIC/host network plane.

sanjay: Applying taint and initiating graceful connection drain on node pool-gpu-az1a. Command: 
```
kubectl taint nodes -l pool=gpu-az1a az1a_problem=tainted:NoSchedule
kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-router --namespace=prod
```

katie: Also temporarily lowering max-concurrency for the inference runtime in az1a to reduce tx bursts: 
```
redwoodctl set config inference.runtime.max_concurrency --region=usw2 --az=az1a 8
```

josh: Fallback model toggle enabled (smaller quantized variant) for routes hitting az1a. This reduces p99 CPU/GPU time and should help egress queue pressure.

aws-support-bot: AWS support case opened (case # 1234567890). Initial note: "Customer reports NIC RX drops and ENI resets affecting instance network plane in eu-west2?" — (automated).

anna_oncall: Correction to AWS note: US West 2 / az1a. Attach logs in the case and request priority review for host NIC/ENI.

maria: Metrics update at +12m: region-wide 5xx down to 0.9%; az1a still ~9% for traffic that remains. Latency p95 for hosted API in region improved from 1.8s -> 1.2s after steering.

cs_ryan: Sent initial customer note. Asking for follow-up timeline.

josh: Infra team reporting repeated ENI reattachments on a subset of instances — suggests host NIC firmware/hypervisor interaction. We should keep nodes drained until AWS confirms.

sanjay: Putting an annotation on the incident: possible root cause: node-level NIC rx queue starvation leading to kernel-driven interface resets, manifesting as connection econnreset and 5xx at the edge.

anna_oncall: Next actions: (A) Keep az1a nodes cordoned/drained. (B) Maintain steering policy to avoid az1a for all new allocations. (C) Continue AWS case; request host-level packet captures if they ask. (D) Prepare rollback plan to reintroduce AZ when ENI stability confirmed.

maria: CS asked for customer impact numbers for the postmortem — can we snapshot request volume, error counts, and the subset of customers pinned to az1a?

josh: Will export logs and produce a CSV: route, tenant_id, request_count, error_count. Share to incident doc.

anna_oncall: Timeline note: incident created 2867004321; steering started +3m; taint/drain started +7m. Continuing to monitor. If az1a error rate does not improve in 60m, move to SEV-1 escalation.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigating, severity=SEV-2, owner=anna_oncall.

katie: Quick perf note — enabling fallback model increased cost slightly but reduced error surface; consider candidate for automatic failover policy.

cs_ryan: Customer update drafted and queued. Will post after you confirm no additional changes.

anna_oncall: Thanks team. Keep updates short in thread. If anyone needs workspace, DM me. :thumbsup:

maria: Logging final for shift: I'll take the handoff if this continues into the next hour.

anna_oncall: Copy that. Handoff pinned to 2867004800 when I hand to maria.

incident-bot: Automatic reminder scheduled in 30m for status check.
